Macomb County Circuit Court is a judicial court that serves Macomb County, Michigan. Established in 1818, the court is responsible for handling a variety of legal matters, including civil lawsuits, criminal cases, and family law disputes. In this article, we will provide a comprehensive overview of the Macomb County Circuit Court, including its history, jurisdiction, and procedures.

History of Macomb County Circuit Court

Macomb County was established in 1818, and the first circuit court was established soon after. The court was originally located in the county seat of Mount Clemens, which remains its location to this day. Over the years, the court has undergone several changes, including the addition of new judges, the expansion of court facilities, and the adoption of new technology to improve court operations.

Jurisdiction of Macomb County Circuit Court

The Macomb County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over a wide range of legal matters, including civil lawsuits, criminal cases, and family law disputes. Some of the most common types of cases heard by the court include:

  • Civil lawsuits involving disputes over money, property, or contracts
  • Criminal cases involving felony offenses, such as murder, robbery, and drug offenses
  • Family law disputes involving divorce, child custody, and child support

In addition to its primary jurisdiction, the court also hears cases on appeal from lower courts in the county.

Procedures of Macomb County Circuit Court

The procedures of the Macomb County Circuit Court vary depending on the type of case being heard. In civil lawsuits, for example, the plaintiff files a complaint with the court, and the defendant must respond within a certain period of time. The court then schedules a trial, during which the parties present evidence and arguments to a judge or jury. In criminal cases, the defendant is entitled to a trial by jury, and the prosecution must prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt.

In family law cases, the court may require the parties to participate in mediation or other alternative dispute resolution methods before proceeding to trial. The court also has the authority to issue orders regarding child custody, visitation, and support, and to enforce those orders through contempt proceedings.

Macomb County Circuit Court Judges

The Macomb County Circuit Court currently has 14 judges, who are elected to six-year terms by the voters of Macomb County. The judges are responsible for presiding over cases, making rulings on legal issues, and overseeing court operations. In addition to their judicial duties, the judges also serve on various committees and task forces aimed at improving the justice system in Macomb County.

Macomb County Circuit Court Services

The Macomb County Circuit Court offers a variety of services to the public, including:

  • Online access to court records and case information
  • Assistance with filing court forms and documents
  • Access to legal resources and referrals to local attorneys
  • Support for victims of domestic violence and other crimes

The court also operates a drug court and a veterans court, which offer specialized services to individuals with substance abuse or mental health issues.
